messages:
Maya (Finance): Quick broadcast: small changes to invoice payment windows and approval routing effective next Tuesday. Please read; highlights below.

Owen (Eng): tl;dr?

Maya (Finance): TL;DR: standard vendor invoices now default to Net 30; exceptions (Net 60/90) need VP Finance signoff. All invoices must include a PO number or procurement ticket ID to be routed automatically. Missing PO -> AP hold.

Claire (Sales): What about strategic partners who historically had Net 45 terms?

Maya (Finance): Strategic partners: Procurement will review existing contracts and create exceptions where justified. If you have partners with legacy terms, ping procurement@redwood.com with contract ID and business rationale.

ProcurementBot: New step: when submitting a PO request, include anticipated invoice cadence and preferred payment terms to speed onboarding. See https://intranet.redwood/finance/invoice-guidance

Owen (Eng): If an invoice hits an AP hold for missing PO, how fast can we resolve it?

Maya (Finance): Typically same-day if the PO/ticket is provided and procurement confirms. If not, AP will hold payment and auto-escalate after 7 days. Finance will notify the cost owner.

Claire (Sales): Will this affect commissionable deals where payment timing matters?

Maya (Finance): Commissions: revenue recognition and commission ops will be informed about holds. If payment timing affects quota/commission timing, flag it in the procurement intake so we can route for expedite.

finance-bot: Reminder: attach PO or procurement ticket to supplier invoices. Missing attachments may result in holds. Link: https://intranet.redwood/finance/invoice-guidance :bell:

Maya (Finance): We also added a fast-track approval for any invoice dispute under $2,000: submit a dispute form and Finance will triage within 72 hours. Larger disputes follow normal resolution.

Owen (Eng): Thanks, useful. Small request: could Procurement post a one-line example of required invoice metadata? That'd cut down on errors.

Maya (Finance): Good call 1 I'll ask Procurement to publish an example and we'll pin it to the finance docs this week. Thanks everyone.
